accuracy.evidence: Checked against the DfE KS3 science programme of study (Biology: 'cells as the fundamental unit of living organisms, including how to observe, interpret and record cell structure using a light microscope', 'the functions of the cell wall, cell membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus, vacuole, mitochondria and chloroplasts', 'the similarities and differences between plant and animal cells') and the AQA GCSE Biology 4.1.1.2 specification for ribosomes and electron microscopy. Every rule in the lab was checked: animal cells have membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus, mitochondria and ribosomes but no wall, chloroplasts or permanent vacuole; leaf palisade cells add all three; root cells have a wall and vacuole but no chloroplasts; mitochondria release (not make) energy by aerobic respiration; the cellulose wall is fully permeable and resists bursting; total magnification is eyepiece × objective (×10 × ×40 = ×400); ribosomes and mitochondrial detail need an electron microscope. Item answers 10o, 0 and o hold at every parameter corner.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets misconceptions documented in the research on pupils' ideas about cells (Dreyfus & Jungwirth 1988; Flores, Tovar & Gallegos 2003; AAAS Project 2061 cells misconceptions list; the RSC/IOP-style KS3 'Best Evidence Science Teaching' cells module): animal cells having a cell wall (step 1 decoys and prediction, tag memb), plant cells lacking mitochondria because chloroplasts supply energy (step 2 prediction, 'already in, mitochondria too' feedback, mastery m2, tag chl), all plant cells having chloroplasts (root-cell build rejects chloroplasts, tags nocell and flower), the wall controlling entry (job feedback, tag wall), mitochondria 'making' energy (tag make), adding lens powers (tags add and div) and a cell bursting with too much water (vacuole step refuses beyond firm and names the wall).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagorganel is built around one drawn cell that the learner assembles from an eight-part tray, then reuses for job matching (the matching part lights up), a light-microscope view whose cell detail appears only as the objective reaches ×40, and a vacuole whose size sets turgor and pulls the membrane off the wall. It differs from the other biology labs (flaggut digestion, flagbreath breathing, flagxylem plant transport, flagbones skeleton) and from every chemistry particle lab; no other lab builds or zooms a cell. The gate reports under 30% shingle overlap with every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers each fact by acting: tapping the cell wall for an animal cell is rejected with the reason before the text says animal cells lack walls; the plant cell starts with every animal part already in, so mitochondria are visibly kept; the root cell refuses chloroplasts; the microscope shows only bricks at ×40 and nuclei and chloroplasts at ×400, so the sort of visible vs electron-only parts follows from what was seen; and adding water stops at 'firm' because the wall holds.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions, each with a tempting wrong option that the lab then disproves: 'Yes: every cell has a wall' (the wall is rejected for the animal cell), 'No: chloroplasts do that job' for plant mitochondria (mitochondria are already in and stay), 'Yes, at ×400' for ribosomes (the ×400 view shows no ribosomes and the sort puts them under electron microscope), and 'It bursts' for a water-filled plant cell (the wall stops further swelling). Each task completion echoes the locked-in choice.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions, two wrong options each, each with its own message: wall (strength, not control), nuc (genes control the cell, the membrane controls the edge), chl (chloroplasts make glucose), vac (stores sap), mito (animal cells need mitochondria; they lack a wall), memb (every cell has a membrane), nocell (all plant parts are cells), flower (chloroplasts are in green parts), add and div (multiply lens powers), make (energy cannot be made) and light (chloroplasts absorb light). Job-matching feedback is specific to the part tapped (e.g. 'Chloroplasts trap light to make glucose. Mitochondria release the energy from it.').

readability.evidence: validate_lessons.py passes the learner limits; the kid paragraphs score about grade 3 and the adult text about grade 7 after the adult paragraphs were rewritten into shorter sentences (the first draft scored 12.9). Technical words (membrane, cytoplasm, mitochondria, ribosomes, chloroplasts, vacuole) are each tied to one plain job, and the canvas uses short titles such as 'Animal cell: 3 of 5 parts' and 'eyepiece ×10 × objective ×40 = ×400'.

no_filler.evidence: No filler pattern matches. Each step has one job (animal parts, plant extras, functions, microscopy, turgor) and every feedback line carries a part name and a reason. Item explanations give the function or the arithmetic (10 × o, total ÷ 10) rather than restating the prompt.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 px width in light and dark, before and after Show me for every step. After the first pass the phone tray changed from four narrow columns (where 'mitochondria' was clipped at 10 px) to three columns at 12 px, the canvas was made taller (1.3 × width) so three tray rows fit above the feedback banner, the microscope sort boxes became two wide half-width boxes instead of tiny tray cells, and the root cell now stays on screen after it is finished. Every tray action is repeated by a full-size button below the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: Every action has a labelled button: 'Add cell wall', 'mitochondria does this job', 'Use the ×40 objective', 'Sort: electron microscope', 'Add water to the vacuole'. After each move the canvas aria-label states the live state, e.g. 'Parts in the cell: cell membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus. Build an animal cell.' or 'Vacuole water level 4 of 4. Now let it go floppy.' Challenge feedback is an aria-live status. walk.cjs reports axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) clean in light and dark on desktop and iPhone 13 with no console errors; the canvas keeps a light card in dark mode.
